title: Telemetry runway and dashboard annotation journal
content:
Purpose:
This is a working notebook for the telemetry runway we want in place ahead of model rollout v2 (quantized + batching changes). The goal: strip down a minimal, high-value set of metrics + trace annotations + dashboard widgets that let oncall and SRE quickly assess whether a rollout impacted latency, token-economics, or correctness signals.

Quick summary / TL;DR:
- Keep metrics small and action-oriented: 8–12 SLI candidates, 6 probe types, 4 dashboard views.
- Trace annotations should be lightweight (3–6 tags) and deterministic so session reconstruction is reliable across multi-hop requests.
- Dashboard widgets must have clear drilldowns (trace link, tenant breakdown, recent prompts).
- Rollout smoke probes (synthetic + real-sample replay) should run on canary for 30m before ramp.

Notes style: informal. TODOs sprinkled. Unresolved items flagged with "Q:"

1) Core metric definitions (candidate set) - compact, action-first
- metric_name: inference.tft.first_token_latency_p50
  description: median time from request ingest to first token emitted (edge of runtime)
  unit: ms
  owner: eng-serving-runtime (Ethan Park)
  alert_hint: p50 increase > 20% for 15m vs baseline and p95 > 200ms absolute
  instrumentation: emit at gateway after routing decision and on model container at token emit; tag: model_version, region, tenant_id, route_id

- metric_name: inference.tft.token_cost_per_k
  description: normalized token CPU/GPU cost equivalent per 1k tokens (unit economics)
  unit: cost_units/1k_tokens
  owner: eng-costing (Lila Rivera)
  alert_hint: sudden upward step > 10% coincident with traffic spike
  instrumentation: derive from per-model token counters + allocation factor; include batching_factor and quant_profile tags

- metric_name: inference.kvcache.warmth_rate
  description: fraction of requests served with warm KV cache prefix (session-aware)
  unit: ratio (0..1)
  owner: eng-serving-runtime (Maya Thompson)
  alert_hint: drop below 0.6 for 30m in high-tier tenants
  instrumentation: boolean emitted from model sidecar: kv_warm=true/false; compute rolling window

- metric_name: inference.output.hallucination_ratio_snap
  description: approx rate of hallucination flagging from automatic QA heuristics (synthetic QA)
  unit: ratio
  owner: research-evals (Omar Singh)
  alert_hint: upward trend > 3x baseline over 60m -> trigger quality-review runbook
  instrumentation: sampled checkers for small fraction of requests; tag: eval_suite, model_version

- metric_name: inference.errors.user_facing_500_rate
  description: client-visible 5xx rate (post-proxy)
  unit: pct
  owner: eng-sre (Jenna Li)
  alert_hint: >0.5% sustained 10m or >1% spike = page oncall
  instrumentation: counted at API edge; tag: route, tenant_id, auth_tier

- metric_name: batching.avg_batch_size
  description: mean batch size observed for model execution windows
  unit: tokens/request
  owner: eng-serving-runtime (Ethan Park)
  alert_hint: fall below configured minimum target for a tier = cost regression signal
  instrumentation: record per-batch emission event from runtime (batch_id, model_version, seq_len_distribution)

2) Trace annotation plan (keep it tiny)
- required tags (emit on root span):
  - trace.annotation.session_id (session provenance for multi-call flows)
  - trace.annotation.request_route (route_id / feature flag variant)
  - trace.annotation.model_version (pinned string)
  - trace.annotation.kv_warm (boolean on span whenever kv cache used)
  - trace.annotation.batch_id (optional, only for batched runs)

Rationale: these five allow us to stitch request -> model call -> token stream -> fallback and measure per-session SLI. Avoid free-form user content in traces (PII).

Annotation semantics and emitter guidance:
- session_id: gateway assigns; stable across retried requests within 5m; use UUIDv4.
- model_version: exact tag used for rollouts (e.g., gptx-13b-q4_202601) to allow time-travel queries.
- kv_warm: emit at model container when prefix match > 0.5; boolean string 'true'/'false'.
- batch_id: opaque short token; include only when batch_size > 1 to avoid noise.

Q: How to handle tool-calls (function/tool spans)? Proposal: propagate request_route + session_id into tool spans; add trace.annotation.tool_name and trace.annotation.tool_latency_ms. Keep tool tags optional to limit cardinality.

3) Dashboard and widget notes (wireframe -> implementation hints)
- View A: Rollout Health Overview (single page)
  widgets:
  - W1: SLI panel (first_token_p50/p95, errors_5xx, kv_warmth) - top-left, 1m resolution, last 6h and 30d sparkline
    drilldown: click -> launches probe timeline + trace query (session_id sample)
    query_hint: anchor to route=canary and global; facet by model_version
  - W2: Cost panel (token_cost_per_k, batching.avg_batch_size) - top-right
    note: show both absolute cost estimate and per-tenant ratio; allow toggle: amortized vs instantaneous
  - W3: Quality snapshot (hallucination_ratio_snap sampled) - center
    on hover: show recent failing prompt examples (redact PII) and link to eval run in research board

- View B: Oncall Investigator (operator-first)
  widgets:
  - W4: Session list (streaming table of recent traced sessions hitting p95 latencies)
    columns: session_id, route, model_version, p95_latency_ms, kv_warm_flag, tenant_id
    action buttons: "open traces", "replay prompt" (replay -> dev sandbox)
  - W5: Trace waterfall sample (inline span visual) for the selected session row; show tool call durations and where fallback occurred

Implementation notes for dashboards:
- All widgets should include trace link macro: trace://?session_id=<id>&span=root
- Limit cardinality on dropdowns: precompute top 50 tenants by QPS and fallback to "other"
- Use a hybrid retention: 1m resolution for 30d for SLIs, raw traces sampled & retained 7d (hot), archive older to 90d with lower fidelity

4) Probes and synthetic tests (practical minimal set)
- Probe 1: canary-synthetic-short (short prompt, 16 tokens expected) -> checks first_token_p50, kv_warm=false expected
- Probe 2: canary-kv-warm (multi-turn replay from production sample) -> expect kv_warm=true for warm sessions
- Probe 3: quality-sanity (synthetic QA questions) -> measures hallucination heuristics and censor rates
- Probe 4: batching-pressure (submit burst of tiny requests to gauge batching.avg_batch_size response)
- Scheduling: run all probes every 30s against canary and every 5m on global; abort ramp if any probe fails 3x consecutively

5) Oncall quickcards (sticky reminders)
- When paged for high latency:
  1) Check Rollout Health Overview -> look at p50 vs p95 and kv_warmth. If kv_warmth drops, suspect cold-cache/regenerator issue.
  2) If errors_5xx high across tenants -> check API edge logs for auth_tier and routing changes; correlate with deploy time.
  3) If token_cost_per_k spikes -> check batching.avg_batch_size and quant_profile tag; roll back quant profile if cost regressions persist.

6) Pruning/cardinality heuristics (we will enforce these)
- Don’t tag traces with free text (user prompt). Use hashed prompt_id if needed for sample replay.
- Maintain explicit allowlist for tenant tags (top 50) and collapse remaining into 'others'.
- For dashboards, pre-aggregate high-cardinality dimensions server-side to avoid query timeouts.

7) Open questions (Q:) and decisions to make
- Q: sampling policy for hallucination checks vs latency traces. Proposal: sample all latency traces for tenants above threshold; sample hallucination QA at 0.1% per tenant, ramp to 1% for high-risk models.
- Q: where to store prompt snippets for replay without exposing PII? Proposal: store redacted prompt + prompt_hash and replay via secure sandbox with access control. Need legal/Privacy signoff (JIRA-1488).
- Q: alert tuning for token-cost spikes that are correlated with batch size reductions vs model changes. Action: create a correlation runbook (JIRA-1356).

8) Next steps (owners & timeline)
- [Maya] finalize required trace tags and publish span-emitter library patch (target: 2026-01-25)
- [Ethan] add metrics emitters for first_token_latency and batching.avg_batch_size to runtime (PR draft: linked_artifacts) (target: 2026-01-20)
- [Lila] wire cost estimator into dashboard and create amortized view (target: 2026-02-01)
- [Omar] prototype hallucination sampler and baseline report (target: 2026-01-28)
- [Jenna] define alert rules and oncall card text (target: 2026-01-22)

9) Quick references and helpful links
- rollout checklist (confluence:OBS-612)
- trace macros and span naming conventions (confluence:trace-naming-v2)
- recent related PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/2145
- privacy ticket: JIRA-1488

Notes / rough sketches:
- Keep the dashboard colors conservative for oncall (red/amber/green, avoid purple gradients).
- If we see correlated p95 latency + kv_warmth drop -> prioritize prefilling KV warm for affected tenant cohorts.
- Prototype the session list as a streaming table to reduce load when investigating spikes.

Misc TODOs (short):
- [ ] finalize probe failure thresholds and wire into canary gate automation (JIRA-1347)
- [ ] draft privacy-safe prompt storage design (JIRA-1488)
- [ ] instrument batch_id emission in runtime and verify cardinality (Ethan)

End of notebook. This is intentionally concise; expand into separate runbook and dashboard PRs once owners confirm instrument changes.
